title: Magnolia Sign, Hospital Wiring, Fines & Fees
summary:
*   **New Commercial Signage & Electrical Safety Rules:** Approved an electric sign for Magnolia Petroleum Co. on Congress Avenue and began developing a new ordinance to regulate all electrical wiring installations, requiring contractor licenses and bonds for public safety.
*   **City Hospital Wiring Fiasco:** Discovered a major wiring mistake in the new City Hospital (wired for 220V instead of 110V), leading to an urgent $212.25 contract to correct the issue and install new underground power lines.
*   **Social Justice & Debt Collection:** Suspended a $31.80 fine for vagrancy for Edna Smith, with the condition she not re-offend. Also, increased the commission for collecting difficult-to-recover old sewer bills from 5% to 10% to incentivize collection.

Regular meeting of the City Council: Austin, Texas Nov 19th

The Council was called to order by the Mayor: Roll called: Present Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Absent none.

The minutes of the last regular and subsequent recessed meetings were read and adopted:
Reports of City Officers:

The Mayor laid before the Council the report of the City Sexton, the Sanitary Inspector,
the Supt of the City Hospital Building, for the month of October 1914, also also those of
the Supt streets, account of General Fund and the Permanent street fund, the Cashier of
the Sewer Plant, for the months of Sept & October 1914 which were read and ordered filed.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: Magnolia Petroleum Co.
Whereas, the application of G Flury, agent for the Magnolia Petroleum Co, to Sign erect an
electric light sign at 917 Congress Avenue in this City has been approved by the Sign
Inspector, W L Eyres Now, therefore, Resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin:
That permit be and is hereby granted by the City Council of the City of Austin, Texas, to
the Magnolia Petroleum Co to erect and maintain an electric light sign at 917 Congress
Avenue in this City, said sign to be in general accordance with the specifications set out
in the petition of the said G Flury, agent, and in all other particulars to be in strict
conformity with the ordinances of this City in this behalf made and provided.
Be it further resolved:
That this permit is revocable at the pleasure of the City Council.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes and Powell 5
Nays none.

Councilman Powell offered the following resolution: Be it resolved by the City Council of
the City of Austin: Final Sewer Payment That the 2 % of the final estimate on sewer
construction contract # 15, amount-ing to $ 72.42, which amount is being held to cover
maintenance expenses, be Johnson & Carr and the same is hereby ordered paid to Johnson &
Carr, the firm contracting for this work.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Electric wiring The Mayor laid before the Council an ordinance amending existing ordinance
ordinances of the City of Austin, regulating the installation, repair opera-tion and
maintenance of all electric wiring, and providing for the licensing and bonding of
electric contractors, and providing penalties.
The ordinance was read the 1st time.


 --- Page break --- 

163
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution: Whereas, it appears from the
report of the City Electrician, and also the Architect in charge of the construction of
the building, that a mistake was made in the size of the wires used for wiring the new
City Hospital building, Now, therefore, Resolved by the City Council of the City of
Austin: That the proposition of the A E Hancock Co to increase the size of all wires and
panel to take care of 110 volts instead of 220 volts, as originally figured, for the price
of $ 32.25, be and the same is hereby accepted.
Be it further resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin: That the proposition of
the said A E Hancock Co, to lay a three inch underground conduit containing one duplex No
6 lead covered cable, and one triplex No 2 lead covered cable, extending from the City's
power lines at the curb north of the new City Hospital under ground and into said building
to the main meters, be and the same are hereby also accepted.
Be it further resolved by the City Council: That the sum of $ 180.00 be and the same is
hereby appropriated out of the General Contin-gent fund of the City of Austin, Texas, to
pay the said A E Hancock Co. for doing the work and supplying the material called for in
the two propositions herein above accepted.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

November 25th 1914. All present:
Councilman Haynes offered the following resolution: Resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin: That the sum of $ 8.90 be and the same is hereby appropriated out of the
General Contin-gent fund of the City of Austin, Texas, as a refund to Mrs Hans Assman upon
retail Liquor dealers license No 641, for the selling of Malt liquor in the City of
Austin, Texas.
Said license was dated the 11th day of July, 1913, and expired on the 11th day of July,
1914. Hans Assman died March 28th, 1914, and the unused portion of said license is $ 8.90,
the amount of this appropriation.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
